chunks: 5144 - And in the narration of Ziyād ibn Marwān al-Qandī, from someone whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
The thief is not subject to amputation in a year of deprivation for anything that is eaten, such as bread, meat, and cucumbers.

key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief, the person accused of theft
key_terms.سَنَةِ الْمَحْقِ: a year of famine, scarcity, or devastating deprivation
key_terms.شَيْءٍ يُؤْكَلُ: something edible, food fit for eating
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: is subjected to amputation as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: Is the thief's hand cut off for stealing food during a famine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the hadd punishment for theft is not carried out during a year of famine or severe scarcity when the stolen item is edible food. It reflects the consideration of necessity and public hardship in the application of legal punishments.
